events.note: Narrative rewritten from the legacy dossier in scanner-neutral language, with citations to evidence sources and contract claims. Drafted with AI assistance (Claude) under the named author; not reviewed. Dossier content that is not carried is accounted for in docs/migration/narrative-report.md.

Statement 'jwt-installation-token' (lifecycle) is recorded as unresolved: The announcement is recorded in a research note, but none of the sources this family's contract cites states it, so no evidence-source record backs the date or the format here.

Statement 'body-and-checksum-current' (openQuestions) is recorded as unresolved: The only provider statement is the prefix and role. The body length and checksum come from a 2021 post that the token-formats page does not repeat, so it is not established that every token of this family issued today follows it.

Evidence review for issue 97 (2026-10-03, automation, not independently reviewed). The lifecycle statement jwt-installation-token, recorded as unresolved at event 2 because no cited source stated the announcement, is now backed by two GitHub changelog entries (2026-04-24 and 2026-05-15) and the token-formats note on docs.github.com, and is re-classed provider-documented. The body-36 statement is scoped to the opaque form. Whether the APPID segment, the stateless length bounds and the rollout end date are documented stays unresolved.

Statement 'app-id-segment-grammar' (shape) is recorded as unresolved: The provider writes the stateless form as ghs_APPID_JWT but documents neither the alphabet nor the length of the APPID segment, nor whether every stateless token carries it; the recommended regex also accepts a ghs_ value without one.
Statement 'stateless-length-bounds' (openQuestions) is recorded as unresolved: The provider says about 520 characters and varying with the token contents, with no stated lower or upper bound.

Statement 'rollout-completion' (lifecycle) is recorded as unresolved: The provider says the temporary header will stop being respected at a date to be announced and that all eligible apps will then receive stateless tokens; no date or completion statement was found on the pages read.

Evidence review for issue 179 (2026-10-04, automation, not independently reviewed). The lifecycle statement rollout-completion, recorded as unresolved at event 7, is now backed by GitHub's 2026-10-02 changelog entry (rollout complete, header deprecated 2026-11-30) and is re-classed provider-documented. The APPID segment grammar, the stateless length upper bound and the current checksum stay unresolved: that entry and the pages re-read add no statement on them.
